newsitem.title: CHINA: China says no HK consulates for Taiwan's allies.
newsitem.headline: China says no HK consulates for Taiwan's allies.

text.p: China said on Tuesday countries that did not have diplomatic relations with Beijing would not be allowed to maintain consulates in Hong Kong after the British colony reverted to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

"It's impossible for countries that do not have diplomatic relations with China to maintain consulates in Hong Kong...after July 1," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.
"In principle they can only maintain non-official...or semi-official institutions in Hong Kong," Shen said.

Such countries should in any case adhere to the "one China" principle and should not engage in the policy of "two Chinas" or "one China, one Taiwan", Shen said, referring to recognition of China's arch-rival, Taiwan.
China and Taiwan have been diplomatic rivals since the Communists won the Chinese civil war and drove the Nationalists into exile on the island in 1949.
Beijing insists it is the sole, legitimate government of all China and has sought to push Taiwan into diplomatic isolation.
"Two Chinas" and "one China, one Taiwan" are Beijing euphemisms for Taiwan independence. China has threatened to invade if the island declares independence.
Taiwan has diplomatic relations with only 30 countries, most of them small, poor and heavily dependent on Taipei's financial largesse.
Shen said Taiwan would be allowed to maintain a civilian institution in Hong Kong after the handover.
